definition: Indic Computing means "computing in Indic", i.e., Indian Scripts and Languages.
details: It involves developing software in Indic Scripts/languages, Input methods, Localization of computer applications, web development, Database Management, Spell checkers, Speech to Text and Text to Speech applications and OCR in Indian languages. Unicode standard version 15.0 specifies codes for 9 Indic scripts in Chapter 12 titled "South and Central Asia-I, Official Scripts of India". The 9 scripts are Bengali, Devanagari, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Kannada, Malayalam, Oriya, Tamil and Telugu. A lot of Indic Computing projects are going on. They involve some government sector companies, some volunteer groups and individual people.

explainer.lead: Indic computing means computing in Indian scripts and languages, covering input methods, localization, and language applications. It matters for making software usable across India's scripts.

tiers.eli5: It's everything needed to make computers work properly in Indian languages and writing systems.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build input methods, spell checkers, speech-to-text and text-to-speech, and OCR for Indian languages. A pitfall is that Unicode currently specifies codes for only 9 Indic scripts, so coverage is bounded.
tiers.paperLevel: Unicode standard version 15.0 specifies codes for 9 Indic scripts in Chapter 12, 'South and Central Asia-I, Official Scripts of India': Bengali, Devanagari, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Kannada, Malayalam, Oriya, Tamil, and Telugu.

explainer.example: A spell checker for Devanagari uses Unicode-encoded characters so text renders and processes correctly across applications.
